summary: San Juan NF lookout in Archuleta County, CO, built by the CCC in 1939 on a stone base; cab removed in 2010, and the site is now in a national monument.

facts.design: one-story stone base topped with a 14'x14' wooden cab with gable roof and catwalk; stone taken from adjacent prehistoric buildings
facts.status_note: Cab removed in fall 2010; register says most of the floor was left in place. No source describes the site after 2010.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (San Juan National Forest)

access.note: Chimney Rock Archaeological Area has guided walking tours May 15 to Sept. 30; sources do not say whether the lookout remains are on the tour route. The register says the site was closed to the public after the falcon listing, with no date given.

events.note: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps as a one-story stone base with a 14x14-foot wooden cab; stone from adjacent prehistoric buildings
Item quoted on a lookout-history site describes a new lookout station built near the historic Chimney Rock; does not match the register's 1939 date
Register says the cab was removed 'in the 1970s'; only the decade is given, so the year here stands for the decade
Cab rebuilt in 1987 for observation of the archaeological ruins
Cab removed in the fall of 2010 by the USFS for archaeological investigation; most of the floor left in place
Registered July 15, 2011 as FFLOS US 1085, CO 16; nominated by Kent Argow
Chimney Rock Archaeological Area designated a national monument on Sept. 21, 2012

evidence.supports: built in 1939 by the CCC as a one-story stone base topped with a wooden cab
evidence.quote: The original one-story stone base topped with a 14'x14' wooden cab with gable roof and catwalk was built in 1939 by the CCC.

evidence.supports: lookout built of stone from adjacent prehistoric buildings, on a 1,000-year-old fire pit
evidence.quote: On the site of a 1000-year-old fire pit, the lookout was built of stone from the adjacent prehistoric buildings.

evidence.supports: site abandoned in 1959; cab removed in the 1970s and rebuilt in 1987
evidence.quote: Abandoned in 1959, the cab portion of the tower was removed in the 1970s and rebuilt in 1987 for observation of the archaeological ruins in the area.

evidence.supports: cab removed in fall 2010 by the USFS
evidence.quote: The cab was removed in the fall of 2010 by the USFS for purposes of archaeological investigation.

evidence.supports: most of the floor left in place to protect deposits
evidence.quote: Most of the floor from the tower was left in place to protect deposits beneath it.

evidence.supports: a 1970s column for a viewing deck appears in the 2010 photo
evidence.quote: The column visible in the 2010 photo was constructed during the 1970s in anticipation of supporting visitors on a circular viewing deck

evidence.supports: deck plan dropped when peregrine falcons were listed; site then closed to the public
evidence.quote: That plan was abandoned when Peregrine Falcons were listed as endangered and the site was closed to the public.

evidence.supports: site located in San Juan National Forest, Archuleta County
1942 item describes a new lookout station built near the historic Chimney Rock
evidence.quote: For better fire detection on the forest a new lookout station has been built near the historic Chimney Rock.

evidence.supports: Chimney Rock Archaeological Area designated a national monument on Sept. 21, 2012
evidence.quote: On Sept. 21, 2012, President Barack Obama designated the Chimney Rock Archaeological Area as America’s 103rd national monument

evidence.supports: guided walking tours daily May 15 to Sept. 30
evidence.quote: Chimney Rock Interpretive Association offers daily guided walking tours May 15 – Sept. 30.

evidence.supports: visitor center cabin open in the same season
evidence.quote: the Visitor Center Cabin is open daily from 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. from May 15 to Sept. 30.

evidence.supports: Colorado list marks the structure as removed (2-Story Cab Removed)
evidence.quote: Chimney Rock Archuleta 37.19190 -107.30582 2-Story Cab Removed FFLOS US 1085, CO 16

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates construction to 1939 by the CCC; a 1942 item quoted on a lookout-history site describes a new lookout station built near the historic Chimney Rock. Both are recorded and the story does not choose.

Forest Service pages describe guided tours in season; the register says the site was closed to the public at an undated time after the falcon listing. The story reports both and does not say whether the closure still applies.

sources.title: Chimney Rock - Forest Lookouts (newspaper items transcribed)

notes_for_editor: The record's kind 'two_story' is kept: the register describes a one-story stone base with a wooden cab, and the Association lists a '2-Story Cab'. No change proposed. The 1970 removal year is a stand-in for 'the 1970s'. The register's 'closed to the public' line has no date, so the story does not state current access beyond the Forest Service tour dates. Staffing is not in the sources and is omitted.
